question.prompt:
Point \(E\) is on side \(AB\) of square \(ABCD.\) If \(EB\) has length one and \(EC\) has length two, then the area of the square is

[Figure 1](figures/1981_AMC_12_Q02_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Since \(E\) lies on side \(AB\) of the square, \(EB\perp BC\). Thus triangle \(EBC\) is right at \(B\), with hypotenuse \(EC=2\) and leg \(EB=1\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
BC^2=EC^2-EB^2=2^2-1^2=3.
\]
The square's area is its side length squared, so the area is already \(\boxed{3}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Find the side squared directly
